notes: The catalogue has no female-to-female jumper type, so the generic `jumper-wire` type is used for the three female-to-female cables.
No breadboard is used. The cables go straight from the PIR sensor pins to the Pi header.

The 5V pin is shown as the top-right pin of the header (physical pin 2), so it is mapped to 5V.1. The GND pin is the one just below it (physical pin 6), so it is mapped to GND.1. Any Pi GND pin would work.
The manual says to use any numbered GPIO pin for OUT and picks GPIO 4. The diagram agrees.
Wire colours come from the diagram: red for VCC, black for GND, orange for OUT.
The manual says to pop the cap off the sensor if the pin labels are hidden. This is a preparation step and not a part.
